author: snokijum
quote:
** Recommended (9/10)**
**127 hours played (and still going strong)**

Crimson Desert has been one of the most enjoyable RPG experiences I’ve had in years. I’m over 100 hours in and only just reaching Chapter 4—not because of padding, but because the game genuinely rewards taking your time. There is a *lot* to do here, and most of it is actually worth doing.

The first thing that stands out is the presentation. The graphics are absolutely stunning, with an incredible level of environmental detail and scale. Whether you're riding across open terrain or stumbling into a dynamic encounter, the world feels alive and worth exploring. The music complements this well—it's not always front-and-center, but it consistently enhances the atmosphere.

Gameplay is where Crimson Desert really shines. Combat is intense, weighty, and satisfying. There’s a clear skill curve, especially with some of the bosses. If you’ve played something like Dark Souls, you’ll feel right at home adapting to a boss's timing, positioning, and learning patterns. It’s challenging and victories feel earned. If a boss feels unfair, it is always because you either need better gear or need to learn their patterns better. If that's too difficult for you, well the game now has an Easy setting, as of the most recent update. It also now has a Hard mode for those who want even more of a challenge.

The side content deserves a lot of credit too. I’ve gone out of my way to complete as many side quests as possible, and most of them are genuinely engaging rather than filler. That’s a rare thing in modern RPGs. There’s a strong sense of discovery here—whether it’s hidden encounters, unique questlines, or just stumbling into something unexpected.

That said, it’s not perfect. One of the more noticeable drawbacks is the repetition in voice lines. After a while, you’ll start to hear the same clips reused, which can break immersion a bit. There are also moments where the game’s systems feel slightly unpolished or overly ambitious, but they don’t significantly detract from the overall experience.

Despite those issues, the sheer amount of content, combined with the quality of exploration and combat, makes this an easy recommendation. I haven’t had this much fun with an RPG since Skyrim, and that says a lot.

**Bottom line:**

If you’re looking for a large-scale RPG with beautiful visuals, rewarding combat, and a world that actually feels worth exploring, Crimson Desert delivers. It’s not flawless, but it gets far more right than wrong—and it’s a game I’m genuinely happy to keep sinking time into.

author: snokijum
quote:
This is the worst game I have ever played.  Seriously.  Absolutely pitiful.  Vomit-inducing gameplay and enough microtransaction "Surprise Mechanics" to make your head spin.  This game doesn't even qualify as minimum effort from the developer, it's worse than that.  Nothing new here from EA, but hey at least there are rainbow-colored coaches this year.  They should have just called this Copy and Paste From Madden 20.  How in 2020 can a game be released in such a horrendous state?
Graphics glitches are everywhere and the physics are seizure-inducing.  Please for the love of God, do not buy this hot dumpster fire garbage of a "game"!  NFL needs to hand the licensing to an actual developer that loves the game of football and cares about its fans.  At this point, that's pretty much anyone except for Electronic Arts.
